Definition: from a compound of G4183 and G3056; loquacity, i.e. prolixity:--much speaking.
BiblicalUsage: Polylogia is much speaking, piling up words in prayer as if God were won over by the volume. Jesus warns against it directly: do not use vain repetitions, as the heathen do, for they think they shall be heard for their much speaking.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that prayer is not a performance measured in words, because my Father already knows what I need before I ask.
